variants.name: E-commerce (Edge Cases)
variants.description: 100 harder questions over the bundled Edge Cases sample, a synthetic e-commerce store (orders, order lines, payments, shipments, returns, reviews, customers, products in a 3-level category tree, inventory snapshots, legacy orders) full of planted data problems: duplicate spellings, NULLs and blanks, odd column names, an empty gift-card table. Select its PostgreSQL datasource with the saved dataset 'Edge Cases'; Settings, Testing Data loads both.

cases.question: Across our eight main departments, how many units have we sold in each, counting sub-categories and their sub-sub-categories under their department? Leave out cancelled orders and any lines with zero or negative quantities.
cases.intent: Must roll the three-level category tree up to the 8 top departments and rank them by units: Electronics first with 661,815 units, Books last with 475,204. Trap: grouping by the product's own category gives 60+ rows; keeping negative/zero lines or cancelled orders changes the totals.
cases.notes:
Verified 2026-11-18 on edge_cases (8 rows, 0.4s). Result (columns as in expectedSql, '|' separated):
Electronics|661815|127561
Apparel|619662|123833
Home|593529|114541
Beauty|591409|113996
Sports|526167|100886
Toys|523127|100321
Grocery|481377|96441
Books|475204|95334
Fixed 2026-11-18: reference trimmed to department and units; the order_lines helper column failed a right answer. Trimmed reference returns: Electronics|661815, Apparel|619662, Home|593529, Beauty|591409, Sports|526167, Toys|523127, Grocery|481377, Books|475204.

expectedSql.postgres:
SELECT COALESCE(gc.name, pc.name, c.name) AS department, SUM(l.quantity) AS units
FROM edge_cases.order_lines l
JOIN edge_cases.orders o ON o.id = l.order_id
JOIN edge_cases.products p ON p.id = l.product_id
JOIN edge_cases.categories c LEFT JOIN edge_cases.categories pc ON pc.category_id = c.parent_category_id LEFT JOIN edge_cases.categories gc ON gc.category_id = pc.parent_category_id ON c.category_id = p.category_id
WHERE o.status <> 'cancelled' AND l.quantity > 0
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY units DESC

cases.question: Which delivery company carried the most shipments for our VIP customers, and how many?
cases.intent: FedEx with 29,981 VIP shipments once 'FedEx' and 'FEDEX ' are treated as one carrier (also 'dhl' as DHL). Trap: without merging the spellings the carriers look equal (~15,000 each); customers whose VIP flag is unknown are not VIPs.

FedEx|29981
UPS|15048
DHL|14999
Servientrega|14963

expectedSql.postgres:
SELECT CASE WHEN LOWER(TRIM(s.carrier)) = 'fedex' THEN 'FedEx' WHEN LOWER(TRIM(s.carrier)) = 'dhl' THEN 'DHL' ELSE TRIM(s.carrier) END AS carrier, COUNT(*) AS vip_shipments
FROM edge_cases.shipments s
JOIN edge_cases.orders o ON o.id = s.order_id
JOIN edge_cases.customers cu ON cu.id = o.customer_id
WHERE cu.is_vip IS TRUE

Trap: raw grouping shows Brazil alone on top with 5,000.
cases.notes:
Verified 2026-11-18 on edge_cases (9 rows, 0.1s). Result (columns as in expectedSql, '|' separated):
Brazil|10000
United States|10000
Canada|5000
Colombia|5000
France|5000
Mexico|5000
Spain|5000
Germany|2500
Japan|2500

Trap query (must return different rows): SELECT country, COUNT(*) FROM edge_cases.customers GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 2 DESC LIMIT 3
Fixed 2026-11-18: reference trimmed to the two tied top counts (10000, 10000) so a country label in another case or spelling (UNITED STATES, USA) and a top-N cut pass; the regex still needs Brazil and the United States, the trap's LIMIT 3 has no 10000 row. Trimmed reference returns: 10000, 10000.

expectedSql.postgres: WITH x AS (SELECT CASE WHEN LOWER(REGEXP_REPLACE(TRIM(country), '[^a-zA-Z]', '', 'g')) IN ('usa','unitedstates') THEN 'United States' WHEN LOWER(TRIM(country)) IN ('españa','spain') THEN 'Spain' WHEN LOWER(TRIM(country)) IN ('méxico','mexico') THEN 'Mexico' ELSE INITCAP(LOWER(TRIM(country))) END AS country FROM edge_cases.customers), c AS (SELECT country, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM x GROUP BY 1) SELECT customers FROM c WHERE customers = (SELECT MAX(customers) FROM c)
